one_liner: Collect, check and summarize company questionnaire and import data for USITC trade-injury investigations, working with economists, attorneys and auditors in DC.
fit_summary: Daniel's people skills, policy knowledge and government-client consulting at IEM match the posting's emphasis on interpersonal skills and dealing with officials and counsel. However, GS-11 requires one year of GS-9-level specialized experience in trade, economic or financial data studies, or a Ph.D./3 years of graduate study in a related field, and nothing on file shows trade data or trade-remedy law work. Apply only if your IEM role involved substantial survey design, quantitative analysis and briefing on findings.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring paths include public, vets and fed-transition), so no federal status is needed.

Basic requirement: related graduate and undergraduate education (economics, business, international trade/relations, etc.), OR experience showing knowledge of goods production in trade, trade competitiveness factors, trade data methods, and U.S. trade laws.

GS-11 specialized experience: one year at GS-9 level conducting trade/economic/financial studies, fact-finding to gather trade data, qualitative and quantitative analysis, and briefing managers. The alternative is a Ph.D., 3 years of related graduate education, or a related LL.M.
Secret clearance required. Expect a background investigation after selection.
All requirements must be met by the November 9, 2026 closing date and clearly shown on your resume.
keywords: trade, economic, financial, and marketing data
strategy: Before applying, confirm honestly whether your IEM work includes 12 months of data studies, surveys, analysis and briefings. If it does not, skip this posting or target GS-7/GS-9 trade, program or policy analyst roles instead.

Frame IEM work in analytic terms if accurate: for example, designing data calls or surveys for government clients, compiling and validating data, analyzing it in Excel, and briefing client managers on findings.
Within the two-page limit, list title, dates, hours per week, and 4-5 bullets that mirror the four specialized-experience elements word for word where truthful.
On the questionnaire, rate yourself only at levels your resume supports, since inflated answers can lead to adjustment or exclusion. Block time for the USA Hire assessment, which is required.
If relevant, include your transcripts to show any economics, international relations or business coursework. Apply well before November 9, 2026; the window is only about 11 days.
Prepare a short writing sample on a trade or policy topic, because the hiring manager may request a writing assessment.
resume_bullets: Designed and distributed [number] data-collection questionnaires to [type of stakeholders] for [client/project], then followed up with respondents to resolve incomplete or inconsistent responses.
Compiled and analyzed [type of data] from primary and secondary sources using [Excel/tool], producing [report/dashboard] that summarized findings for [client agency] leadership.
Briefed [audience, e.g., client program managers] on study findings and recommendations as a member of a [size]-person research team, [result if known].
interview_questions: Tell us about a time you collected data from outside parties who were slow or reluctant to respond. How did you get complete, accurate information?
Describe an analysis you built in spreadsheets: what data you used, how you checked it, and how you presented it.
What do you know about antidumping, countervailing duty, or safeguard investigations and the Commission's role in them?
How would you objectively summarize conflicting data submitted by a petitioner and a respondent?
watch_outs: The GS-11 qualification bar is high. Without demonstrable trade or economic data experience or a related Ph.D./graduate education, you will likely be rated ineligible.
Knowledge of U.S. trade laws and microeconomic concepts is a rated competency, and the policy knowledge on file is not specifically trade-focused.
A Secret clearance is required. The position is in-office in DC with telework, which means a Manassas commute on non-telework days.
The application window is short (October 29 to November 9, 2026) and requires the separate USA Hire assessment.
